result.title: Optimal Correction Sets for Provable Redress of Contestable Causal Discovery
result.summary: Constraint-based causal discovery relies on conditional-independence (CI) tests that may conflict in finite samples, leaving no causal graph that satisfies them all. Causal Assumption-based Argumentation (ABA) makes these tests explicit as defeasible commitments, and offers correspondence guarantees with a subset of them, but its existing repair procedure releases facts heuristically and offers no formal response to a user's contestation of a release. We argue that contestable causal discovery requires an inspectable repair object, a justification for it, and a predictable revision procedure for such contestations. We therefore formulate CI-fact repair as a minimum-cost correction problem and implement it in Answer Set Programming (ASP). Building on Causal ABA, we provide a compact and efficient ASP encoding of causal consistency, with soundness and completeness guarantees, and a two-way projection correspondence between optimal stable models and minimum-cost correction sets. These results establish fidelity to retained facts, subset-minimality and cost optimality of the repair, conflict-based justifications for released facts, and formally guaranteed redress under user contestations. An empirical evaluation supports the formal account: OptABA-PC retains more correct facts, reduces ambiguity in the compatible outputs, and improves graph reconstruction over Causal ABA on common benchmarks.

AI.brief_summary: 论文把约束式因果发现中相互冲突的条件独立检验事实的修复表述为最小代价修正问题，用 Answer Set Programming 实现，并证明其最优稳定模型与最小代价修正集之间的双向投影对应，从而为用户质疑提供可检查的辩护与形式化纠正保证。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「可检查的修复对象＋基于冲突的辩护＋最小代价修订」框架，可能为 LVR 中相互冲突的视觉证据筛选与信念状态修订提供问题表述和评价思路，但跨领域迁移需较多核查。
